title: Answering all your questions about Megan Thee Stallion as Zidler in M...
transcript: I just saw Megan Thee Stallion's debut performance in Moulin Rouge on Broadway, and here are all of my thoughts, as well as some of the changes that were made in order to accommodate a female Zidler. And let's just get this out of the way right up top. Can she act? Not really. Can she sing? Not really. But did I have a really great time? Absolutely. And I will give her credit, her comedic timing is actually really solid. Her razor scene genuinely had me cackling. And while she's definitely not a vocalist, you don't really need to be for Zidler. She gets by just fine talk singing her lyrics. The one bit they modified for her was chandelier, where she starts off the song talk singing, and then once they get to the chorus, Toulouse takes over and she just kind of mouths the words along with him. Honestly, it worked fine. I should also note that the character's name is now just Zidler. No more Harold, and any references to his first name have just been removed. She does use she her pronouns, so this is an explicitly female Zidler. She's not playing the role as a guy. And I actually really liked the implications of a female Zidler. It made the relationship between Satine and Zidler feel very sisterly. And you get the sense that when the Duke threatens to send them all back out to the street, that that includes Zidler. Very much get The sense that she comes from the same upbringing as Satine and is just trying to do whatever it takes to not go back to that life. Now, there is a queer element of the character, where Zidler flirts with one of the chorus boys. That role is still played by a man, so it is straight in this version. And they did a great job updating the costumes to fit a female body. Like, she has some great looks throughout the show, especially in Act 2. Like, the costume designer really knocked it out of the park, and overall, I had a really fun time. Like I said, she's not technically the best performer, but she really owns that stage and makes the role her own, and I think fans of hers are going to have a really great time.
reasoning: Reviewer acknowledges Megan Thee Stallion's acting and singing limitations but repeatedly emphasizes having a great time, praises her comedic timing, stage presence, and the production's adaptations. Net recommendation with clear caveats.
